newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Dow Chemical CEO says steady profit forecast okay.
newsitem.headline: Dow Chemical CEO says steady profit forecast okay.

text.p: The Dow Chemical Co chief executive officer, William Stavropoulos, said on Tuesday that analysts forecasts of steady earnings for the company in the fourth quarter from a year earlier were "pretty accurate."
Dow Chemical earned $415 million in the fourth quarter of 1995, or $1.63 per share. Sales were $4.59 billion.
Stavropoulos, who is also president of the company, was visiting Singapore to announce its near term plans for Asia, which include investment of about $300 million.
Stavropoulos told Reuters analysts were predicting fourth quarter 1996 earnings similar to those of the fourth quarter of 1995.
"They're pretty accurate," he said while declining to make a direct forecast.
Dow Chemical reported a net income of $469 million, or $1.92 per share, for the third quarter. Earnings for the whole of 1995 were $2.07 billion, or $7.72 per share.
In October, Dow Chemical Chief Financial Officer Pedro Reinhard seemed slightly more optimistic about the fourth quarter.
"While higher feedstock costs in the U.S. will continue to dampen results somewhat, we expect to see higher comparisons for the fourth quarter versus last year," he said.
"Our strategy is on track and 1996 should be another good year for Dow."
Dow Chemical last traded in New York on Monday at 79 1/8, down 3/8 on the day.
